_about: E14 full-episode-only keys. sortDrill, privacyPanel and flipDefenderLineByChoice are pasted by the wiring agent into the FULL erb's social.awarenessEpisode (flipDefenderLineByChoice under .strings). The generator (gen_e8_e17_shells.py DEFEND_HALF_KEYS = sortDrill, concernForm, privacyPanel; defend_half_keys / defend_only) copies sortDrill and privacyPanel from this file into the generated defend-only shell, so edits here reach the defend erb on regeneration. flipDefenderLineByChoice is not copied (the defend-only shell has no flip). Exception: the FULL erb's privacyPanel.note is hand-authored (Dani/board framing) and intentionally differs from the self-framed note here. None of these blocks is compared by the parity test.

sortDrill._notes: Goes in the FULL erb social.awarenessEpisode.sortDrill (ENG-11; shape: sort-drill-model.js normaliseConfig). Runs inside the defend stage as an unscored teaching sub-activity, opened before the scored inbox. scored:false, so it records placements for analytics only and shows no mark (per-card `acceptable` applies to scored drills only; an array answer lists several fine bins). The generator copies this block verbatim into the defend-only shell (DEFEND_HALF_KEYS), so keep the full erb copy in step by hand. Answer balance: post x2 (pet, clean desk), tweak x2 (lanyard, whiteboard), hold x3 (system, leave, school). Each card's reason is the one line of feedback.

strings.title: Post or Not?
strings.heading: Post, Tweak or Hold?
strings.intro: Each card is a draft post. Decide whether to Post it, Tweak it first, or Hold it back. The reason shows straight after.

cards.situation: A selfie for your work anniversary, with your lanyard and pass clearly in shot.
cards.reason: Lovely photo. Crop or blur the pass first: a badge in a photo helps someone copy it or tailgate in.

cards.situation: 'Buried in the new finance system this week but getting there!'
cards.reason: Hold this: naming an internal system tells an attacker exactly which cover story to use. Keep the system out of it.

cards.situation: A team photo at your desks, with a whiteboard of client names and go-live dates behind you.
cards.reason: Post the people, not the whiteboard. Client names and dates in the background are a free briefing for anyone watching.

cards.situation: 'Two weeks off from Friday, can't wait. House-sitter sorted, cat's in charge.'
cards.reason: 'Away for two weeks' tells work who is short-staffed and tells strangers the house is empty. Hold it until you're back, then share the photos.

cards.situation: A photo of your dog on a walk, posted to connections only, no work or location in it.
cards.reason: This one's fine: no work details, no badge, no location, and your audience is set to people you know. Post away.

cards.situation: A 'my desk setup' photo: new chair, a plant, the monitor switched off and nothing else in shot.
cards.reason: Post away: the screen is off and nothing readable is in shot. That is the fixed version of a desk photo; an open inbox or client file on screen can leak names, subjects and even a meeting link.

cards.situation: Your child's first-day photo, tagging the school by name and location.
cards.reason: Hold this one. A school name is a common security-question answer and tells strangers where your child is each morning. Share it with family privately instead.

privacyPanel._notes: Goes in the FULL erb social.awarenessEpisode.privacyPanel (ENG-13; shape { settings:[{ id, label, closesFacts:[se_intel_*], default }], note }). Runs inside the defend stage as an unscored, view-only teaching panel over the OSINT board: toggling a setting marks its named found fact(s) closed. Every closesFacts id names a declared se_intel_<factId> from attack.json's intelFacts. The generator copies this block (settings and the self-framed note below) into the defend-only shell (DEFEND_HALF_KEYS); the defend fact rows come from EPISODES['e14']['defend_intel_facts'] in the generator.

settings.label: Set your profile and work details (employer, team, manager) to connections only
Set new and old posts to connections only, and hide your connections list
Don't name internal systems; take down the reposted job advert
Check the background before posting; crop out badges and screens, and turn off location tags
Use a made-up security-question answer kept in your password manager, not your real pet's name

privacyPanel._note_defendOnly: MA2 (E14_DESIGN_C1): this note is the one the GENERATOR copies into the defend-only shell, which has no OSINT board and no Dani, so it is self-framed (second person, no 'board', no 'Dani'). The FULL erb keeps its own board/Dani-framed note ('Each change closes a found fact on the board. Tighten Dani's profile first, then do the same on your own.'), which is coherent there because its OSINT stage introduces Dani; that erb copy is intentionally NOT regenerated from here. privacyPanel is not checked by the fragment<->erb parity test, so the divergence is safe.
privacyPanel.note: Each switch closes one of the things an attacker could piece together about you from a public profile. Tighten these on your own profile.

flipDefenderLineByChoice._notes: Goes in the FULL erb social.awarenessEpisode.strings.flipDefenderLineByChoice (erb-only; allow-listed in the parity test's STRINGS_ERB_ONLY_OK, so it needs no new allow-list entry). aw2: the built defender-inbox flip reads the chosen pretext templateId and shows the matching line in place of strings.flipDefenderLine. Keys are the pretext template ids in attack.json. The defend-only shell has no write/flip stage and does not carry this key.
flipDefenderLineByChoice.df_pretext_access_now: Yasmin read it between two things. It named Dani's leave, the new system and Thandiwe, so it fitted the week, and the rush left no room to check. When a message fits the week, a colleague acting on it is the ordinary thing to do.
flipDefenderLineByChoice.df_pretext_access_calm: It named a week she knew Dani was away and asked one easy favour, so Yasmin set the access up without a second thought. The ease is exactly what slipped it past her.
